repository.autoCreateFiltersDescription: Without filters, every new issue opens one. "Minimum events" waits until the issue has happened that many times.

issue.unlinkFailed: Could not unlink the GitHub issue

account.title: GitHub username
account.description: Assigning you an issue in Rustrak assigns you its linked GitHub issues, and the other way round.
account.saveFailed: Could not save your GitHub username

setup.title: Set up GitHub
setup.createDescription: GitHub shows you the app before creating it, and it stays private to your account or organization.
setup.organizationHint: Leave it empty for your personal account. The app can only be installed where it is created.
setup.installDescription: Install the app and pick the repositories Rustrak may read.
setup.linkTitle: Link each project to its repository
setup.linkDescription: In each project’s settings, under GitHub.

features.codeDescription: Open the line that failed, at the commit that ran it.
features.commitsDescription: The commit that most likely broke it, on the issue.
features.issuesDescription: Open or link issues, and resolve errors from commits.
features.ownersDescription: Who owns the failing code, from CODEOWNERS.

crons.title: Crons

empty.title: Monitor your scheduled jobs
empty.description: Rustrak tells you when a cron job doesn't run on time, fails, or runs longer than it should. Add a check-in to your job: its monitor is created on the first run.
empty.upsertNote: This example checks in to the my-job monitor every hour and creates it on the first run. Change the slug and the schedule to your job's.
empty.orManual: Prefer to set it up by hand?

checkIn.title: Add a check-in
checkIn.description: Paste the snippet into your job. Your DSN is already filled in.

run.title: Run the job
run.description: Its monitor is created on the first check-in, with the schedule it sends.

alert.title: Get notified
alert.description: Rustrak tells you when a run is missed, fails or takes too long.

setup.copyUnavailableHint: Select the {label} snippet and copy it by hand.

detail.waitingDescription: Missed runs are only detected once the job has checked in at least once. Add one of these to your job:
detail.mutedBanner: This monitor is muted: failures are still recorded but open no issue and send no alert.
detail.failures: {count, plural, one {# failed check-in} other {# failed check-ins in a row}}
detail.successes: {count, plural, one {# successful check-in} other {# successful check-ins in a row}}
detail.inWindow: Of the runs in this window
detail.durationHint: How long the runs took on average, by environment
detail.timelineHint: Each tick is the worst run of its slot, on the same axis for every environment
detail.instrumentHint: Check in from your job with one of these

actions.deleteDescription: Its check-ins are deleted with it; the issues it opened stay. A job that keeps checking in with a schedule creates it again.

form.newDescription: Tell Rustrak when your job should run, and how late or long is too much.
form.editDescription: A new schedule applies from the next check-in. A job that sends its own monitor_config overwrites what it sends.
form.name: Name
form.slugHint: The slug your job checks in with. Taken from the name when empty.
form.slugLocked: Jobs check in with this slug, so it cannot change.
form.marginHint: How late a check-in may arrive before the run counts as missed.
form.maxRuntimeHint: How long a run may stay in progress before it counts as timed out.
form.failureThresholdHint: Failed check-ins in a row before an issue opens.
form.recoveryThresholdHint: Successful check-ins in a row before the issue resolves.
form.previewNote: Times in {timezone}. Each run counts as missed {margin, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} after its time.

crons.search: Search monitors, or filter by state:

legend.timeout: Timed out (over {count, plural, one {# min} other {# min}})
legend.missed: Missed (no check-in within {count, plural, one {# min} other {# min}})

schedule.crontabHint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week. Aliases such as @daily work too.

preview.title: Next runs
preview.empty: Enter a valid schedule to see when it runs.
preview.invalid: This schedule can't run. Check the crontab.

oauth.title: {client} wants to access your Rustrak account
oauth.canDo: If you approve, it will be able to:
oauth.canRead: Read your projects' issues, events, performance data and logs
oauth.canAct: Act on them with your permissions: resolve, comment, change settings you can change
oauth.warning: Only approve if you started this from that assistant. You can disconnect it at any time in Settings → AI assistants (MCP).
oauth.failedDescription: The assistant sent an authorization request Rustrak could not verify, so nothing was shared. Start the connection again from the assistant.

detail.latencyHint: p50 and p95 over the window

detail.slowestHint: Open one to see its trace
